papers.title: Nonlinear Canonical Transformations for Studying Spin-1/2 Hamiltonians
papers.abstract: Strongly correlated quantum systems, including frustrated spin lattices, remain challenging for conventional coupled-cluster methods because their ground states often exhibit strong multireference character and symmetry breaking. Although multireference and symmetry-projected coupled-cluster theories are promising, they are not yet black-box methods and require system-specific development. The XXZ and $J_1$-$J_2$ spin models provide demanding benchmarks. Spin-BCS-based coupled-cluster methods may require high excitation ranks to recover the exact ground-state physics in strongly correlated regimes. We introduce a nonlinear spin-fermion-spin (SFS) transformation designed to map a strongly correlated spin Hamiltonian into a new spin Hamiltonian whose ground state is more accurately described at the mean-field level. For a representative SFS transformation, we identify a compact Clifford circuit that maps transformed product states to circuit-dressed, generally entangled states in the original representation. The transformed Hamiltonian can then be treated using broken-symmetry mean-field theory and post-mean-field methods. Benchmarks for the XXZ and $J_1$-$J_2$ Hamiltonians show that spin mean-field theory in the transformed representation reduces the energy error relative to conventional spin-BCS mean field. The spin-BCS-based coupled-cluster calculations for the one-dimensional XXZ model provide substantially improved accuracy relative to the corresponding untransformed methods. In 2D, the accuracy of the transformed mean-field solutions depends on the site ordering and boundary conditions, as nonlocal strings can appear. These results show that exact transformations of operator representations can serve as many-body preconditioners for mean-field and low-rank coupled-cluster approximations to strongly correlated spin systems.

papers.title: Unrestricted Binary Tree State for the Fermionic Hubbard Model
papers.abstract: Binary tree states have been introduced as compact correlated pair wave functions that improve upon the antisymmetrized geminal power by adding variational flexibility. Here, we extend the binary tree state to the fermionic half-filled Hubbard model using restricted and unrestricted orbitals. Although the ansatz is seniority zero in its optimized pairing basis, its expansion in the original Hubbard site basis can contain nonzero site- seniority character, while unrestricted orbital optimization provides additional flexibility through independent spin-up and spin-down orbitals. This provides a mechanism for a paired ansatz to describe the singly occupied configurations that dominate the repulsive Hubbard model at large U/t. We find that unrestricted BTS closely approaches optimized DOCI in the repulsive regime, substantially improves upon AGP, and reproduces DOCI density correlations more accurately than pCCD

papers.title: Emergent altermagnetism in (LaVO$_3$)$_n$/(LaNiO$_3$)$_m$ superlattices from interfacial charge transfer and octahedral tilts
papers.abstract: Using first-principles calculations, we show that altermagnetism emerges in (LaVO$_3$)$_n$/(LaNiO$_3$)$_m$ superlattices, with $(n,m) = (1,1), (2,2)$ and $(2,4)$, from the interplay of interfacial charge transfer and octahedral tilts. Charge transfer drives the system towards the V$^{4+}$ and Ni$^{2+}$ configuration, turning the otherwise paramagnetic nickelate layers into a magnetically active sublattice. The resulting $C$-type antiferromagnetic order, combined with $a^-b^+c^-$ or $a^-b^-c^-$ octahedral tilts, links opposite-spin sublattices only through nonsymmorphic operations, yielding a $d$-wave spin splitting without spin-orbit coupling. Within DFT+U, the splitting reaches 118 meV in the insulating (LVO)$_1$/(LNO)$_1$ superlattice, about twice that calculated for bulk LaVO$_3$, and decreases as the nickelate layers become thicker. Our findings indicate that this splitting is hosted by both the V and Ni sublattices, with nearly half of its weight on oxygen $2p$ states through $p$-$d$ covalency. Interfacial charge transfer thus emerges as a \textit{design} principle for engineering altermagnetism in oxide heterostructures.

papers.title: Extreme competition between stripes and superconductivity in the hole-doped Hubbard model
papers.abstract: The two-dimensional Hubbard model was originally proposed as the minimal model of uniform $d$-wave superconductivity in the cuprate high-temperature superconductors, but recent calculations with relevant parameters in a realistic doping regime have often found other ground states. Further, uncertainty remains over such results due to the intrinsic bias of different computational methods. Here we address this uncertainty through state-of-the-art neural tensor network and neural backflow state simulations, enabled by large-scale GPU computation, that together reach an unprecedented variational accuracy on lattices with up to 1024 sites. At $1/8$ doping in the pure Hubbard model, as well as with next-nearest-neighbor hopping relevant to the hole-doped cuprates, we reveal a near degeneracy among a low-energy uniform $d$-wave state, superconducting stripes, and non-superconducting stripe states on the milli-$t$ energy scale. Our work rebalances the narrative that the Hubbard model supports a single dominant order in relevant parameter regimes towards a picture of extreme competition between stripes and superconductivity.

papers.title: $π$-Flux Tuning of Quantum Paramagnetism in the Triangular-Lattice Hubbard Model
papers.abstract: We compare two time-reversal-symmetric triangular-lattice Hubbard models at half filling: the zero-flux model and a staggered $π$-flux model with zero and $π$ flux through oppositely oriented triangles. Although both reduce to the same Heisenberg model at leading order in the strong-coupling limit, their distinct charge fluctuation profiles yield different quantum paramagnetic regimes. Combining a strong-coupling expansion with infinite density matrix renormalization group (iDMRG) calculations, we find that the positive ring-exchange of the zero-flux model promotes spontaneous chirality, consistent with its notion of a chiral spin liquid at intermediate coupling. In the staggered-$π$-flux model, whose noninteracting limit is a Dirac semimetal, the ring exchange changes sign and disfavors chiral order and we find no resolvable scalar chirality. This renders flux-tuned ring-exchange an efficient discriminator between chiral and non-chiral quantum paramagnets at finite coupling.

papers.title: Charge Density Waves and In-Gap States in Coupled Chains and Moiré Superlattices
papers.abstract: Charge density waves (CDWs) arise from the interplay between electrons and lattice distortions and are a hallmark of low-dimensional systems. Here we study coupled Su-Schrieffer-Heeger chains, both lattice-matched ladders and lattice-mismatched moiré superlattices, and find a rich set of CDW phases together with symmetry-protected bound states. In lattice-matched chains, the competition between electron-phonon coupling and interchain tunneling drives a sequence of CDW phases, including staggered dimers, trimers, and incommensurate states. These phases are generally gapped and host bound states protected by crystalline symmetries rather than chiral symmetry, and are therefore not pinned to zero energy. Lattice mismatch further reconstructs these phases into long-period supermoiré CDWs, with an ordered array of defects, pinned to the moiré length scale, that host localized electronic states. Interchain tunneling and lattice mismatch thus emerge as natural control parameters for CDW order and bound states in one-dimensional chains.

papers.title: Discrete time liquids
papers.abstract: Discrete time crystals exhibit robust subharmonic oscillations, spontaneously breaking the discrete time-translation symmetry of a periodic drive. Since their emergence, the question of whether other types of temporal many-body order can exist has attracted considerable attention. Here we identify discrete time liquids -- a new form of spatiotemporal order characterized by short-range temporal coherence as a result of time-solitons. We study a two-dimensional spin system coupled to a finite-temperature cavity, whose fluctuations provide a noisy, approximately periodic drive with only finite temporal coherence. Remarkably, the spins nevertheless form a metastable state with robust period-doubled dynamics over an extended parameter regime. Unlike a time crystal, this state has only finite temporal coherence: individual trajectories stochastically switch between the two symmetry-related temporal configurations of the period-doubled response. We identify these switches as time-solitons: topological defects in temporal order that preserve local period doubling while destroying long-range temporal coherence, thereby producing the time liquid state. We propose a minimal model which reproduces the distribution of temporal correlations of the many-body system, suggesting a general description of the time liquid as a time crystal with a finite density of time-solitons. Because these solitons can occur at arbitrary times, ensemble averaging restores continuous time-translation symmetry, raising the intriguing possibility that discrete time liquids can exist in thermal equilibrium.

papers.title: Maxwell-Chern-Simons-Matter in AdS$_3$
papers.abstract: We study Maxwell-Chern-Simons theory on AdS$_3$ coupled to $N$ complex scalars or Dirac fermions, including sextic and Gross-Neveu interactions, respectively. First, we derive the bulk Maxwell-Chern-Simons propagator, clarifying how Dirichlet boundary conditions fix the contributions of the massive and flat sectors. Upon coupling to the matter sector, we work at large $N$ with $κ=k/N$ and $α=Ne^2$ fixed, where $k$ is the Chern-Simons level. We determine the corresponding phase diagrams, and we resum matter insertions to obtain the photon propagator at leading order in large $N$, exactly in $α$ and $κ$. Its poles determine the spin-one boundary spectrum, split into two helicity sectors by the Chern-Simons interaction. With Dirichlet boundary conditions, the unHiggsed scalar phase contains a protected chiral current, which is lifted by Higgsing. In the fermionic phases, the current persists for nonzero effective Chern-Simons level, with helicity determined by the induced level shift. At bulk conformal points, we extract large-$N$ BCFT data for the critical and tricritical scalar theories, as well as for the regular fermion and Gross-Neveu theories.

papers.title: Nature of the bosonic edge phase in a double quantum spin Hall insulator
papers.abstract: Field-theoretic analysis has predicted that the edge of a double quantum spin Hall insulator (DQSHI) can undergo an interaction-driven transition from a phase with fermionic edge modes into one with only bosonic modes. All single-fermion edge excitations are gapped in this bosonic edge phase, but fermion pairs remain gapless, leading to distinct experimental signatures. We numerically simulate the interacting DQSHI edge and verify the existence of the bosonic edge phase. This calculation requires an explicit bulk embedding of the DQSHI edge, due to its mixed anomaly between charge and $S^z$ conservation. We hence employ segment DMRG on an infinite two-dimensional cylinder, where the DQSHI bulk is modeled in terms of two copies of the spin-up lowest Landau level, combined with their time-reversed counterparts. We find that interactions can open a single-fermion gap at the DQSHI edge while fermion pairs remain gapless, matching the predictions for the bosonic edge phase. We find the scaling of the single-fermion gap with interaction strength to be consistent with field-theoretic calculations, and discuss the relevance of the bosonic edge phase to twisted homobilayers of WSe$_2$ and MoTe$_2$. We elaborate on the methodological extension of the segment geometry used here to other topological phases with edge anomalies.

papers.title: Defect flows from functional relations in the asymptotic semiring
papers.abstract: We study perturbations of topological defects by a relevant holomorphic defect field in two-dimensional conformal field theory. This produces translation invariant defects and these necessarily flow to topological defects in the infrared. Translation invariant defects form a monoidal category which extends the fusion category of topological defects. We argue that the renormalisation group flow defines a semiring homomorphism from the semiring of translation invariant defects to an "asymptotic semiring" which we construct from topological defects. The semiring homomorphism preserves functional relations, and we illustrate in the example of Virasoro minimal models that the resulting relations in the asymptotic semiring constrain the defect flow endpoints. The companion paper [1] contains a detailed study of such defect flows in several minimal models, both numerically and analytically.

papers.title: Reentrant $d=2+1$ Superfluidity at High Temperature
papers.abstract: We present a UV-complete model with a global $U(1)$ symmetry in $d=2+1$ dimensions that exhibits a Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless (BKT) ordered phase at arbitrarily high temperatures. A careful separation of scales yields a two-dimensional Euclidean effective field theory whose construction remains perturbatively controlled even when its soft modes become strongly coupled. We determine the BKT phase boundary by carefully matching this theory to existing lattice Monte Carlo results. The high-temperature phase supports gapless static modes and algebraically decaying correlations even as $T\to\infty$.

papers.title: Twisted scattering from Chern-Simons theory
papers.abstract: We consider boundary conditions of two-dimensional Dirac fermions which preserve a non-anomalous continuous symmetry which acts differently on the left- and right-movers. Such boundaries are equivalent to topological defects of Weyl fermions preserving the symmetry. We give a general construction of such defects for conformally-embedded symmetries using Chern-Simons theory. They always exist and can be realised as half-space gauging defects for some finite categorical symmetry. Using this technology, we compute the twist lines to which fermions become attached upon scattering through the defect, the boundary central charge of the corresponding folded boundary state, and its mod-2 valued SPT class. As applications, we first consider abelian symmetries and find agreement with known results in the literature. We then study a novel example where an $SU(2) \times SU(4) \times U(1)^2$ symmetry is preserved. In contrast to the abelian case, the twist lines are intrinsically non-invertible and belong to either a $\text{TY}(\mathbb{Z}_3 \times \mathbb{Z}_3)$ or $\text{Rep}(\mathbb{S}_3) \times \mathbb{Z}_3$ symmetry depending on whether scattering is to the left or the right.

papers.title: AnyonWiki.org
papers.abstract: The AnyonWiki is an open-source project that provides full algebraic and numerical data of fusion and unitary modular fusion categories as a resource for the scientific community. It comes with a database, the AnyonWikiDatabase, that currently includes the classification of multiplicity-free pivotal (braided) fusion categories through rank 7 and more than 25000 fusion rings including the classification of multiplicity-free fusion rings through rank 10, with work in progress to expand. This data is available through AnyonWiki.org, a website that provides robust search and download functionality and presents each fusion ring and category via a dedicated webpage. In this short article we discuss the data available at AnyonWiki.org as well as the scientific and communal motivations for the design of its underlying AnyonWikiDatabase, which are centered around making the data accessible, independently verifiable, granularly citable, useful, and easy to work with.

papers.title: Projective symmetry groups beyond spin-$1/2$: Classifying integer-spin quantum spin liquids
papers.abstract: Wen's projective symmetry group (PSG), introduced a quarter of a century ago, reduced the classification of symmetric quantum spin liquids to an algebraic problem and has guided the study of spin-$1/2$ models and materials ever since. Many current candidate materials and quantum simulators, however, have spin-$1$ or larger moments, and no comparable classification exists for them. We formulate the PSG for fermionic partons of arbitrary spin $S$. Integer and half-odd-integer spins already differ in their gauge structure. Half-odd-integer spins give the familiar $\mathrm{SU}(2)$, $\mathrm{U}(1)$, and $\mathbb{Z}_2$ invariant gauge groups, while integer spins give a different hierarchy that includes $\mathrm{U}(1)\rtimes\mathbb{Z}_2$ and $\mathbb{Z}_2\times\mathbb{Z}_2$; the latter has no spin-$1/2$ counterpart. Three lattice-independent results follow for integer spin. Singlet pairing of the partons is odd under site exchange. A lattice symmetry can exchange the particle and hole representations of the local constraint, which forces symmetry-related sites into opposite constraint sectors. And a time-reversal-symmetric $\mathrm{U}(1)$ state with the same constraint on every site can be gapped only if the number of sites per unit cell is a multiple of $2S+1$. We apply the formalism to the spin-$1$ diamond lattice, realized in frustrated A-site spinels, and find ten fully symmetric Ansätze up to second neighbors. In the $J_1$-$J_2$ Heisenberg model at the mean-field level, the ground state depends on how the constraint is imposed. With the particle and hole representations, the lowest states are fully gapped $\mathrm{U}(1)$ states whose two sublattices sit in opposite constraint sectors, and one of them is gauge equivalent to a paired Ansatz. The classification provides a starting point for integer-spin quantum spin liquids on other lattices and in other materials.

papers.title: Stabilizing and detecting electron fractionalization in the Hofstadter-Hubbard model
papers.abstract: Motivated by the recent progress in correlated Chern insulator physics in moiré systems, we investigate the half-filled triangular-lattice Hofstadter--Hubbard model and its electron fractionalization. Among various competing non-magnetic states, increasing the orbital flux stabilizes and broadens the $\mathrm{U}(1)_2$ chiral spin liquid phase in the Mott regime. In this exotic regime, the electron is fractionalized into gapped spinons and gapped chargons, whose effective bands are linked to the orbital flux. The convolution of the narrow spinon bands with the gapped chargon excitations produces rich and discernible structures in the electron spectral function and the density of states. These results not only identify the orbital flux as a control parameter for the detailed patterns of electron fractionalization and the nature of the Mott transition, but also provide the key spectral characteristics for the angle-resolved photoemission and scanning tunneling studies of the relevant systems, linking the free-particle band topology to intrinsic topological order in the correlated regime.

papers.title: Unambiguous determination of the THz conductivity in driven YBa$_2$Cu$_3$O$_{6+x}$
papers.abstract: Mid-infrared pump, THz probe experiments in YBa$_2$Cu$_3$O$_{6+x}$ yield evidence of a high-temperature transient state of the material with the optical properties of a superconductor. However, there are ambiguities in the extracted transient c-axis THz optical properties, primarily resulting from the sublinear growth of the THz response with increasing mid-infrared pump fluence. It was proposed that this effect may be related to saturation of the material's response, which would then perturb its spatial profile and lead one to overestimate the induced change in the transient optical properties. Yet, sublinear growth of the signal could also arise from other effects unrelated to saturation, for example from a change in reflectivity or deposition depth for the pump pulses. Here, we remove this ambiguity by experimentally measuring the fluence-dependent complex optical constants at the 15-20 THz frequencies of the pump. We show that the observed sublinear growth is to be attributed in large part to the enhanced reflection and reduced penetration depth of the pump field at high fluences. When taking into account these findings, we confirm the original interpretation of a light-induced superconducting state both qualitatively and quantitatively.

papers.title: Charge Density Wave transient states induced by ultrashort hard X-ray pulses
papers.abstract: The interaction of quantum systems with ultrashort laser pulses may lead to transient states far from equilibrium. Among these, Charge Density Wave (CDW) systems offer very rich non-equilibrium physics when submitted to ultrashort optical excitations in the infrared regime. In this Letter, we show that CDW systems pumped by ultrashort x-ray pulses excite the system in very different way. The x-ray pump, 6000 times more energetic than a laser pulse, pumping and probing the whole bulk system simultaneously, drives CDW systems in a novel reversible out of equilibrium state. The successive CDW states observed in the NbSe$_3$ system with respect to the arrival of x-ray pulses follow a non-thermal kinetic path. It is characterized by a change in 2k$_F$ wavevector, correlation lengths and electronic gap, as well as a change of dimensionality, all of this takes place within a very long recovery time ranging from 450$ns$ to 0.01$s$. Several scenarios are proposed, including transient nucleation and recombination of charged topological objects.

papers.title: Quantum criticality in a two-component two-dimensional nematic metal
papers.abstract: Nematic fluctuations alter the low-energy electronic behavior and reshape the mean-field phase diagram. We study a two-dimensional nematic metal with a two-component internal degree of freedom. Near the quantum critical point (QCP), longitudinal nematic fluctuations generate the non-Fermi-liquid self-energy $\propto|ω|^{2/3}$, whereas transverse fluctuations give a subleading logarithmic, marginal-Fermi-liquid correction. Nevertheless, the transverse sector dominates the correction to the phase diagram through a quantum order-by-disorder mechanism: the emergent nematic background reshapes the electronic spectrum, alters the decay of nematic bosons, and produces a negative singular free-energy correction. This correction reconstructs the phase diagram, drives the transition first order, and is described by a scaling function whose two asymptotic limits define two critical regimes with free-energy corrections scaling as $R^{8/3}$ and $R^3$, respectively, where $R$ is the order-parameter magnitude; their powers follow from the competition between the characteristic momentum of normal-state nematic fluctuations and that of the ordered-state background. These two regimes are experimentally distinguishable through nematic-susceptibility hysteresis measurements. The corrected phase diagram shows that the enlarged nodal $α$ phase masks the otherwise bare QCP, making it inaccessible; consequently, the logarithmic self-energy correction is by no means negligible at low energies.

papers.title: Intertwined complex orbital order and ferrimagnetism in honeycomb molybdate Fe$_2$Mo$_3$O$_8$
papers.abstract: Motivated by the recent experimental interest in honeycomb molybdates A$_2$Mo$_3$O$_8$, we return and develop the minimal models to capture the essential physics for Fe$_2$Mo$_3$O$_8$. It is pointed out that, the magnetism in these materials arises from the mutual induction between the spin-orbit coupling of the tetrahedral sublattice with active orbitals and the superexchange with the spins from the octahedral sublattice. Essentially, the superexchange between the tetrahedral and octahedral sublattices directly drives the ferrimagnetism, and the residual spin-orbit coupling on the tetrahedral sublattice induces the complex orbital order. The hybrid magnon-phonon excitations are further explored together with their resulting Berry curvatures and thermal Hall effect. We discuss the experimental relevance with Fe$_2$Mo$_3$O$_8$, and the framework can be extended to FeNiMo$_3$O$_8$, Ni$_2$Mo$_3$O$_8$ and other isostructural magnets.

papers.title: Spin order and excitations in the collinear kagome antiferromagnet Y$_{0.5}$Fe$_3$Sn$_3$
papers.abstract: Kagome lattices host rich magnetic, topological, and transport phenomena owing to their geometric frustration and strong spin correlations. Here we present a systematic neutron scattering study of the kagome metal Y$_{0.5}$Fe$_3$Sn$_3$, which orders into a collinear $c$-axis antiferromagnetic (AF) state below $T_N =$ 551 K. An additional anomalous Hall effect (AHE) contribution beyond the conventional magnetization-scaling response is observed well below $T_N$ under an in-plane magnetic field $\mathbf{B} \parallel ab$. Elastic neutron scattering demonstrates that the Fe moments preserve their collinear $c$-axis AF alignment down to 1.5 K at zero field. Inelastic neutron scattering reveals a distinctive Y-shape spin excitation dispersion exhibiting a two-gap structure below 10 meV, likely arising from two nondegenerate spin-wave branches. Polarized neutron measurements further show that the low-temperature spin excitations are strongly anisotropic: the in-plane component $M_{ab}$ dominates while the $c$-axis component $M_c$ is nearly absent. Upon warming, $M_c$ gradually grows markedly but remains much weaker than $M_{ab}$ even at 300 K. We propose that the unconventional AHE originates from a nonzero scalar spin chirality induced by field-driven spin canting either in the static or dynamic configurations due to gapless excitations. These findings establish the collinear AF kagome metal Y$_{0.5}$Fe$_3$Sn$_3$ as a platform for chirality-driven AHE without spontaneous spin reorientation.

papers.title: Confirmation of complex non-collinear Fe(II) spin ordering in the iron oxychalcogenide La$_2$O$_2$Fe$_2$OSe$_2$ by broad range $^{139}$La-NQR
papers.abstract: The transition metal oxychalcogenide La$_2$O$_2$Fe$_2$OSe$_2$ exhibits a non-collinear spin-ice like antiferromagnetic ordering below $T_N \approx $ 90 K due to complex magnetic exchange interactions and axial single-ion anisotropy of Fe$^{2+}$ spins. The magnetic structure was deduced/determined from combined $^{57}$Fe Mössbauer spectroscopy and $^{139}$La-NMR on polycrystalline specimen. In this work, we present zero-field $^{139}$La-NQR investigations on polycrystalline La$_2$O$_2$Fe$_2$OSe$_2$ in a broad frequency and temperature range between 2.8 - 20 MHz and 4.2 - 100 K. The measured resonances at $ν_Q$, $2 \, ν_Q$, and $3 \, ν_Q$ are fully consistent with the previous NMR studies and also with the magnetic structure. A substantial modification of the electric field gradient at the La-position below $T_N$ is inconsistent with the current investigations.

papers.title: On thermal Hall effect in boson systems
papers.abstract: We theoretically discuss the thermal Hall effect (THE) in boson systems keeping in mind possible applications to magnetically ordered insulators with skyrmion lattice ground state. The magnon spectrum of such systems may undergo a topological transition upon the variation of magnetic field, and THE could be a tool to confirm this phenomenon. We rederive formulas, suitable for our purposes, and find expressions which have a different temperature dependence of THE as compared to previously reported results. Particularly, in presence of anomalous terms in magnon Hamiltonian the thermal Hall conductivity has a small but finite residual 1/T contribution. Such contribution may become sizable at very low temperatures and resembles Meissner effect in superconducting metals.

papers.title: Chiral-Nematic Lattice Instability in Charge Density Wave of 1T-TiSe2
papers.abstract: Chiral charge-density waves (CDWs) are a rare form of electronic order with handedness, enabling novel couplings among light, lattice, and topology in quantum materials. Yet the microscopic origin of chirality has remained elusive, even in the prototypical chiral CDW system 1T-TiSe2. Using ab initio calculations, we investigate the structural stability and electronic structure of competing CDW models in 1T-TiSe2. We show that a chiral monoclinic (C2) structure is stabilized by the cooperative condensation of multiple phonon modes and reproduces the chiral topography and energy gap observed experimentally. We further find an exceptionally soft potential landscape around this energy-minimized structure, along the direction that removes the remaining rotational symmetry, allowing the lattice to fluctuate through fully asymmetric configurations while its average structure remains chiral. This dynamical chiral CDWnaturally reconciles the chiral domains seen by time-averaged topographic probes with the complete loss of symmetry detected by bulk spectroscopy, and clarifies how chiral CDWs emerge from the interplay of lattice instability and fluctuation.

papers.title: Hybridization-Induced Enhancement of the Thermoelectric Response in the Kagome Material CsCr$_6$Sb$_6$
papers.abstract: Flat bands in kagome lattices provide a prominent route to strongly correlated electronic states. Here we report charge and thermal transport measurements on single crystals of CsCr$_6$Sb$_6$, a kagome Kondo system arising from the hybridization between flat and dispersive bands. The Seebeck coefficient and Nernst signal increase rapidly below $T_\mathrm{F}\sim70$ K, concomitant with the emergence of short-range antiferromagnetic correlations and flat-band resonance. The Nernst coefficient in the intermediate-temperature range of $\sim30-80$ K further follows the universal scaling reported for prototypical heavy-fermion compounds, consistent with the development of strongly renormalized quasiparticles associated with hybridization. Both the Seebeck and Nernst responses reach extrema at a lower temperature $T_\mathrm{p}\sim20-25$ K, where phonon drag and correlated quasiparticles may both contribute. These results reveal a hybridization-induced enhancement of the thermoelectric response and establish CsCr$_6$Sb$_6$ as a kagome platform for probing flat-band-derived Kondo physics through thermoelectric transport.

papers.title: Quantics tensor trains for multiloop functional renormalization group in multiorbital impurity models
papers.abstract: The full frequency dependence of electronic interactions is central to dynamical correlations, but its numerical cost restricts multiorbital calculations. We formulate the multiloop functional renormalization group directly in the quantics tensor train representation, retaining all three independent vertex frequencies over broad ranges without an explicit high-frequency parametrization. Analytical tensor operators perform frequency transformations and internal summations without dense vertex intermediates. Multiloop corrections improve agreement of vertices and responses with independent references and reproduce the low-energy numerical renormalization group self-energy. Lower-temperature calculations resolve a quadratic frequency contribution to the analytically continued scattering rate. A degenerate two-orbital impurity exhibits distinct spin, orbital, and charge responses at fixed Hund coupling. In a compensated altermagnetic environment, an orbital-level splitting induces a local spin response despite zero magnetization of the unperturbed impurity. Increasing Hund coupling suppresses the orbital response while increasing its spin polarization. Renormalized one-particle propagation alone does not reproduce this strong polarization dependence. These results extend compressed multiloop calculations to dynamical correlations in multiorbital environments.

papers.title: Ab Initio Approach for Quantum Magnets with Coupled Cluster and Transcorrelation
papers.abstract: The nearest-neighbour exchange coupling $J_1$ is the simplest ingredient of model Hamiltonians used to understand magnetism in real materials. Nevertheless, its ab initio determination requires a high-level correlation treatment and a large basis for wave function expansion. Here we compute $J_1$ for five oxygen-bridged spin-1/2 quantum magnets --- Sr$_2$CuO$_3$, La$_2$CuO$_4$, NdNiO$_2$, ZnCu$_3$(OH)$_6$Cl$_2$, and Li$_2$CuO$_2$ --- spanning bridging angles from 180$^\circ$ to 94$^\circ$ and the crossover from antiferromagnetic to ferromagnetic coupling, using embedded-cluster methodology. To describe the open-shell singlets we use 2-determinant coupled cluster with single and double excitations, which recovers the orbital-breathing enhancement of superexchange from a minimal reference. Basis-set errors are found to be large: extrapolation to the complete basis-set (CBS) limit shifts $J_1$ by up to 50 meV from bases of double-$ζ$ quality. Transcorrelated Hamiltonians reproduce the CBS estimates with modest basis set sizes, yielding an excellent accuracy against experiment at highly affordable cost. These results are the first application of transcorrelated methods in strongly correlated solid-state systems, and establish transcorrelation as a powerful theory in computational research of materials.

papers.title: Chirality, Klein duality, and the stability of Kitaev spin liquids on the star lattice
papers.abstract: The star lattice hosts the Yao-Kivelson chiral spin liquid, an exactly solvable Kitaev spin liquid that breaks time reversal spontaneously and is non-Abelian or Abelian depending on the ratio of its two couplings. A density-matrix renormalization group study found that an added Heisenberg exchange leaves it a wide stability window for ferromagnetic but only a narrow one for antiferromagnetic Kitaev coupling. Using projective symmetry groups (PSGs) of fermionic partons, we show that the chirality is not a peculiarity of the solvable point: whenever the $π$ spin rotations act on the partons as in the exact solution (spin-gauge locking), a time-reversal-symmetric mean-field state has no amplitude on the triangles, at any range, so a Kitaev-type spin liquid on this lattice must break time reversal. The Abelian and non-Abelian liquids of both signs share a single chiral PSG, within which their transition is a band inversion. The Klein duality, which reverses the Heisenberg coupling, permutes the PSGs and leaves exactly the locked ones unchanged; a $Z_2$ spin-liquid phase mapped onto itself is therefore locked and, if it spans a connected range of couplings, contains a Kitaev point. Unprojected mean-field theory in Kitaev's Majorana representation treats both signs alike. Exact second-order perturbation theory about the Kitaev points locates the asymmetry: the triangles respond identically for both signs, whereas on the bonds between triangles the two off-diagonal Heisenberg terms create the same four visons and interfere constructively for antiferromagnetic and almost destructively for ferromagnetic coupling, admixing a low-energy four-vison state $82$ times more strongly on the antiferromagnetic side. The PSG results rest on a classification of $352$ $Z_2$ PSGs with spin-orbit-coupled amplitudes, which also identifies the fermionic partners of the known Schwinger-boson spin liquids.

papers.title: Interplay of disorder and phonons in two-dimensional transport
papers.abstract: We calculate the temperature- and density-dependent resistivity of bilayer MoSe$_2$ in the presence of charged impurities, short-range defects, and longitudinal acoustic phonons, using the Boltzmann transport theory with screening treated in the random phase approximation, and compare the results with recent transport measurements. The disorder parameters are taken from the experiment itself and the phonon parameters are taken from literature estimates for MoSe$_2$. We find that screened acoustic phonons are a small correction to the disorder-limited resistivity over the entire experimental temperature range, so that the temperature dependence of the measured resistivity on the metallic side is controlled by the temperature-dependent screening of charged disorder and by neutral defects. We also show that a resistivity minimum as a function of temperature can arise on both sides of the metal-insulator crossover through two different mechanisms: on the insulating side from the interplay between activated carriers and resistive scattering, and on the metallic side from the interplay between disorder and phonon scattering. The existence of a resistivity minimum by itself therefore does not identify the phase.

papers.title: Valence-Driven Structural Transformation and Phase Coexistence in Chemically Substituted EuPd2Si2
papers.abstract: EuPd2Si2 serves as an ideal system to probe the interplay between lattice dynamics and electronic instabilities through its tunable valence transition, responsive to temperature, pressure, and magnetic field. Here, we focus on investigating the origin of the temperature-induced europium valence instability in pristine EuPd2Si2, alloyed EuPd2Si1.95Ge0.05, and EuPd2Si1.9Ge0.1 and its correlation with structural responses. Compared with the parent compound EuPd2Si2 which exhibits the europium valence transition at Tv = 143 K, magnetic susceptibility measurements reveal a systematic shift in Tv with Ge substitution, decreasing to 87 K for EuPd2Si1.95Ge0.05. Temperature-dependent synchrotron X-ray diffraction confirms phase coexistence between Eu2+Pd2Si2-xGex and Eu3+Pd2Si2-xGex phases across the valence transition for all samples measured (x = 0, 0.05, 0.10). The pronounced increase in the full width at half maximum (FWHM) well above Tv reflects the gradual nature of the transformation and highlights the role of structural strain in stabilizing the coexisting phases, supporting the presence of a phase-segregated ground state, in contrast to a homogeneous intermediate-valence or mixed-valence state. The variation in Tv across different compositions correlates with changes in lattice parameters, highlighting the robust coupling between the structural and electronic degrees of freedom. The phase diagram suggests an inverse linear relationship between the lattice parameter and Tv, suggesting a possible predictive framework for estimating transition temperatures in other chemically substituted variants of this family.

papers.title: Memory--Transport Competition in Physical Two-Bath Quantum Reset Dynamics
papers.abstract: Coherence preservation and environmental renewal offer competing ways of controlling quantum memory and transport. We show that a seemingly natural protocol which exactly replaces the bath occupations while preserving arbitrary system--bath coherences need not correspond to a physical fermionic state. We instead construct a two-reservoir protocol with independent, number-conserving thermal attenuators, for which complete positivity and fermionic admissibility hold by construction. Physical attenuation necessarily modifies bath populations as well as cross correlations; the coherence control is not an independent hard-reset knob. Quadratic dynamics reduces the stroboscopic problem to an exact matrix fixed-point equation without a weak-coupling or Markov approximation. Analytically, coherence retention enhances the leading short-cycle transfer rate, including the complete-erasure limit; no general endpoint-vanishing theorem exists. An exact stationary continuity theorem forces the through-current to vanish whenever either reservoir is left entirely unrefreshed, although no analogous theorem suppresses it at complete erasure. For biased structured reservoirs, exact finite-chain calculations display distinct coherence-, current-, and signed energy-transfer operating points; a resolved high-retention boundary layer exposes strong finite-size sensitivity of the coherence peak. The model provides a microscopic, fermion-admissible benchmark for the interplay of reservoir coherence, particle transport, and energetic exchange.

papers.title: Non-adiabatic Optimisation via Localisation-Delocalisation Transitions
papers.abstract: The promise of efficiently solving classical optimisation problems on quantum computers is tantalizing. As many such problems can be mapped to approximating the ground state of spin-glasses, paradigmatic models for studying many-body localisation, it is natural to ask if some of the intuition coming from quantum statistical mechanics can help guide the construction of novel quantum optimisation algorithms. In this work, we discuss how continuous reverse quantum annealing crossing a many-body localisation transition can be accelerated by considering the density of Landau-Zener crossings as the system is quenched. We provide an interpretation of this behaviour in terms of an effective Fokker-Planck equation for the success probability of the algorithm. This interpretation suggests an improvement in the required annealing time as a function of the system size $N$, which goes from $\mathcal{O}({\rm poly}(N))$ to $\mathcal{O}(1)$ for reference states with non-vanishing energy density. We show that the continuous dynamics can be Trotterised with a number of steps that remains modest as system size increases, making it appealing for near-term devices. For the resulting circuit implementation, we provide a quantitative strategy for determining the parameters of the time-dependent Hamiltonian. We compare the performance of our digitised algorithm, which we call FRIO, against that of the QAOA for finding the ground state of spin-glass problems, in particular the SK model. The numerical results suggest that with suitably selected circuit parameters which can be efficiently found using thermalizing dynamics, FRIO almost always outperforms the conventional QAOA ansatz with pre-optimized angles.

papers.title: The role of locality and weight sharing in convolutional neural networks
papers.abstract: The success of convolutional neural networks is often attributed to locality and weight sharing. However, how these two properties separately shape learning, and how their effects depend on the spatial correlations of natural images, remain poorly understood. We address these questions in a teacher-student model with a convolutional teacher acting on $P$ input positions with correlation $c$ between positions. We compare convolutional and locally connected students trained by online stochastic gradient descent, and derive ordinary differential equations that describe their dynamics exactly in the limit of large feature dimension $D$. For uncorrelated positions ($c = 0$), the two students follow the same learning trajectory, with the convolutional student learning exactly $P$ times faster. We also find that locality affects the sample complexity: a student that matches the kernel size of the teacher recovers it from $\mathcal{O}_{D}(D)$ samples, whereas $\mathcal{O}_{D}(D\log(D))$ samples are needed with a larger kernel. For $c > 0$, spatial correlations can reduce the advantage of weight sharing. The asymptotic error of the convolutional student grows with $c$, whereas that of the locally connected student is independent of $c$ and overall lower when evaluated at the same learning rate. When the learning rate is instead tuned to the training horizon, however, the locally connected student wins at early times and the convolutional student at late times, with a transition that we predict analytically.

papers.title: Stockmayer Fluid with a Shifted Dipole. III. Ion Solvation
papers.abstract: Though ion solvation is well understood for the standard Stockmayer fluid, the effect of displacing the point dipole of a Stockmayer particle, a simple geometric modification, on ion-solvent structuring and solvation thermodynamics remains less understood. We use molecular dynamics simulations to describe how a dipole shift affects radial and orientational solvent structure around centered ions, how strongly the solvent distinguishes cations and anions, and how the solvent mediates ion-ion pairing. We show that, with a centered dipole, cations and anions have equal preferences for the local solvent environment. Shifting the dipole breaks the fore-aft symmetry of the local electrostatic field, leading to a stronger preference for a Stockmayer particle's dipole to orient towards an anion and a weaker preference to orient away from a cation. These structural asymmetries propagate to the solvation free energies: increasing dipole displacement makes anion solvation more favorable, while cation solvation becomes less favorable overall across dipole strengths. The same asymmetry also manifests in the effective ion-ion interaction-increasing the dipole shift reorganizes the local solvation environment, enhancing solvent shielding of short-range cation-anion contact while weakening screening at longer range. As a result, solvent-separated configurations become comparatively more favorable, whereas increasing dipole strength produces the opposite trend. Such effects cannot be explained by bulk dielectric screening alone, indicating that molecular charge geometry plays an important role in both single-ion solvation and solvent-mediated ion-ion interactions. This work demonstrates that dipole location, not only magnitude, provides a geometric control on ion-specific solvation and ion pairing in general polar fluids.

papers.title: Hydrodynamic description of correlation matrix eigenvalues in a finite temperature expanding free fermionic gas
papers.abstract: A recent work considered the Page curve for entanglement entropy of a freely expanding one-dimensional Fermi gas starting from a finite box (the system) in a zero-temperature initial state that then expands in to a semi-infinite vacuum (the environment). For the case with a single defect at the system-environment junction, it was shown that the Yang-Yang entropy of the system computed from semiclassical hydrodynamics agrees with the microscopically computed entanglement entropy, yielding the Page curve. On the other hand, the environment Yang-Yang entropy showed a monotonic increase. Here, we propose a hydrodynamic description to obtain the eigenvalues of the microscopic correlation matrix for a nonzero temperature freely-expanding Fermi gas. For the system, the phase space density directly gives the correlation matrix eigenvalues and thus, via the Yang-Yang formula, yields the von-Neumann entropy. For the reservoir, a modification of the phase space density is required in the Yang-Yang formula, to incorporate coherences, in order to reproduce accurately the entropy. The hydrodynamic description of correlation matrix eigenvalues also leads to a Levitov-Lesovik type formula for the full-counting-statistics for a finite system in the transient regime. We provide a heuristic derivation of the correlation matrix eigenvalues based on a semiclassical wave-packet picture.

papers.title: Generalized Coordinate Bethe Ansatz and Quantum Integrability of the Time-Dependent Massive Thirring Model
papers.abstract: We develop a generalized coordinate Bethe-ansatz framework for the massive Thirring model with an explicitly time-dependent fermion mass. Unlike the generalized Bethe ansatz for chiral quantum field theories, where particle transport acts in internal spin spaces and leads to quantum Knizhnik-Zamolodchikov equations, the present construction acts directly on particle coordinates and physical rapidities. Its central new feature is a rapidity lattice. Because the time-dependent mass couples right- and left-moving components already in the one-particle sector, a fixed-rapidity block is not closed under spatial winding. Periodicity therefore requires all sectors generated by the finite shift $β\toβ-p$. Particle exchange relates amplitudes on this lattice through scalar analytic difference equations of Ruijsenaars type, whose solutions determine the complete time-dependent many-body wavefunction. Consistency of the coordinate construction also selects an exponential evolution of the bare mass, providing a new realization of the time dependent integrability-renormalization group correspondence. In the static limit, the rapidity-lattice construction reduces to the conventional massive-Thirring Bethe equations. Through the massive-Thirring/sine Gordon equivalence, the result also connects this exact quantum construction to the generalized space-time dependent Lax formalism.

papers.title: Morphological instability and negative geometric friction from contact with active and driven particles
papers.abstract: Overdamped particles on a deformable substrate induce a geometric friction through their response to metric perturbations. Nonequilibrium dynamics couples such a perturbation to kinetic effects, which can flip that friction negative, softening the substrate's rigidity and favoring invaginations and evaginations. A breathing circle, with local curvature radius as dynamical variable, is the main example. At equilibrium the friction reduces to an ordinary potential response and stays positive. Geometric response emerges as a new route by which active and driven matter reshape their environment.

papers.title: Closing of density wake in concentrated colloidal suspensions: two regimes governed by compressibility, friction, and self-propulsion
papers.abstract: When an obstacle moves through a compressible medium, it creates a density perturbation. Theoretical arguments regarding the shape of this density wake in Brownian suspensions either suppose infinite dilution or describe only the far field. Here, we study via experiments and numerical simulations the closing of the density perturbation just behind a circular obstacle in dense 2D suspensions of particles that are thermal or self-propelled. In the thermal case, we show that the characteristic length of the wake is a non-monotonic function of density, decreasing then increasing. We rationalise the scalings of both regimes by analytical arguments that highlight the role of the compressibility factor of the suspension. Based on this new understanding of the passive case, we show that the influence of self-propulsion observed in experiments and simulations can be understood as if the obstacle is effectively larger in an active bath, with non-trivial and distinct roles of the self-propulsion velocity and of the persistence time.

papers.title: Energy-fed commitment: a minimal model of random selection followed by reinforcement
papers.abstract: When a symmetric instability is crossed, fluctuations choose one of several equivalent branches. We study a minimal stochastic model of what can then make that choice progressively harder to undo. After selection, the stiffness of the selected state grows in proportion to the energy released each time the structure recovers from a perturbation; in this conservative model that energy equals, up to small and explicitly computed terms, the work absorbed from the perturbing agent. The model is a phenomenological closure with one coupling constant. That energy reinforces a branch already chosen, rather than choosing it, is an assumption of the model, which we state and do not derive. Its consequences are quantitative. The growth of commitment depends on how the structure is driven: geometric under displacement control, linear under energy control and sublinear under force control, so that committed states absorb more work per cycle under displacement control and less under force control. Reinforcement suppresses reversal exponentially; beyond a finite commitment the alternative minimum disappears and reversals become rare crossings of an irreversibility threshold. With unbounded reinforcement a choice is retained forever with positive probability under stated conditions; with saturating reinforcement retention is finite, with a lifetime that grows exponentially with the saturation level. Exact first-passage calculations agree with stochastic simulations; these verify the closure and its analysis but cannot test the physical postulate. We identify the experiments that could: protocols that separate absorbed energy from the number of perturbations, and driven steady states with nonzero housekeeping heat, in which heat and absorbed work differ.

papers.title: Mechanism of delayed elastic state absorption versus fatigue failure in cyclic shear of amorphous materials
papers.abstract: We study cyclic shear in a lattice elastoplastic model of amorphous materials. The model displays a threshold shear amplitude $γ_{\rm c}$, which increases with sample annealing. For imposed amplitudes $γ_0\lesssimγ_{\rm c}$, it shows slow progression to an absorbing elastic state. For $γ_0\gtrsim γ_{\rm c}$, it shows slow fatigue and delayed material failure. Our key contribution is to elucidate a mechanistic understanding of this behaviour. We show that progression to an absorbing state maps to single element diffusion on a finite interval with two absorbing boundaries. We derive expressions for the decay rate of the fraction of active elements, and the survival distribution. The diffusing variable is the local elemental strain, which takes two jumps stroboscopically per cycle. Once the value at any site diffuses below its yielding threshold, the element behaves elastically. This leads to a gradual accumulation of strains just below threshold. For $γ_0\lesssim γ_{\rm c}$ this diffusive behaviour is preceded by many cycles in which cooperativity between elements via stress propagation is also important. For $γ_0 > γ_{\rm c}$, stress propagation dominates and precipitates failure. For $γ_0\gtrsim γ_{\rm c}$, the same accumulation of elements just below local threshold that led to an elastic state for $γ_0\lesssimγ_{\rm c}$ accounts for the fatigue that brings the system to the brink of failure. We evidence this via simulations in which the strain amplitude artificially exceeds $γ_0 $ in each half cycle, before reverting to the system's actual state at $\pmγ_0$ and resuming the next half cycle. During fatigue, the stress-strain slope $dσ/dγ$ evolves towards unity at $|γ|=γ_0^-$, signifying perfect elasticity within cycle, yet towards zero at $|γ|=γ_0^+$, precipitating failure.

papers.title: Stochastic resonance in time-delayed bistable active particles
papers.abstract: We investigate analytically and numerically stochastic resonance in an underdamped active (Ornstein--Uhlenbeck) particle confined in a bistable potential with time-delayed feedback and subjected to an additional (non-thermal) white-noise source. Restricting the analysis to the active-noise-dominated bistable regime, with sufficiently short delay and active-noise correlation times, we develop a perturbative theory that yields analytical expressions for both the escape rate and the spectral power amplification within the framework of linear-response theory, without invoking detailed balance. The analytical predictions are in qualitative agreement with direct numerical simulations throughout the perturbative regime. We show that a moderate increase in the active-noise correlation time can enhance the stochastic-resonance response, in marked contrast to previous results for overdamped passive systems driven by colored noise. Conversely, the addition of white noise weakens the resonant response and shifts its optimum toward lower active-noise intensities. Time-delayed feedback further alters the matching condition between the escape rate and the driving frequency while preserving the resonant mechanism. Beyond the perturbative regime, we find that finite-memory effects progressively broaden the resonance profile and substantially decrease its amplitude. Overall, these results provide new insight into the combined role of inertia, activity, environmental fluctuations, and time delayed feedback in stochastic resonance in nonequilibrium systems.

papers.title: Splitting Probability in Monitored Quantum Dynamics
papers.abstract: We consider a continuous-time quantum walk stroboscopically subjected to projective measurements on two distinct targets with sampling time period $τ$. We construct a general renewal framework for the first-detection amplitude at each target, from which we obtain the associated splitting probabilities. For Hamiltonians with reflection symmetry, we further show that each dual-target first-detection amplitude can be viewed as an interference effect between a pair of single-target first-detection amplitudes. This formulation yields exact expressions for the splitting probabilities and gives special sampling times at which they undergo pointwise discontinuous jumps due to a form of ergodicity breaking associated with dark states. As an illustrative example, we apply the framework to a one-dimensional tight-binding lattice chain with nearest-neighbor hopping, and study the splitting probabilities as functions of the initial position and sampling time. Below a critical sampling time, $0<τ< τ_c$ where $τ_c = 2 π/ ΔE$ with $ΔE$ being the energy bandwidth, the splitting probabilities for large system sizes become equal to $1/2$, independent of the initial position, as long as this position does not coincide with target sites. Above the critical sampling time, $τ\geq τ_c$, the splitting probabilities deviate from $1/2$ and develop oscillations as a function of initial position. The wavenumber associated with these oscillations is $Q=2\sin^{-1}(rτ_c/τ)$, where $r$ is a positive integer. We also explore the effects of relative phase and spatial separation between different components of a coherent initial state on the splitting probabilities. Finally, we study how a finite number of measurements modifies the splitting probabilities and broadens the resonances at special sampling times.

papers.title: Phase Transitions in Learning Driven by Extremal Data
papers.abstract: We study an extremal regression problem, an example of multiple instance learning (MIL), where the predictors are given as multisets, called bags. The bag elements (called instances) possess hidden labels which are pooled to produce an observed bag-level label. Max pooling is common in MIL applications, but gives rise to vanishing gradients. To handle this, modern MIL pipelines approximate the max with a softmax, treating the sharpness as a learnable parameter, denoted $λ$. When the max pooling model is the true data generating process, learning will be successful when $λ$ is increased during gradient descent, thereby driving the dynamics into regions of parameter space with vanishing gradients. To understand the conditions under which gradient descent breaks down, we study a minimal model and derive a low dimensional projection of the gradient flow in the joint limit of large bags $n$ and high dimension $d$ with $α=\ln n/d$ fixed. The flow has two distinct phase transitions: an intrinsic freezing transition related to the random energy model of disordered systems, and a retrieval transition occurring in modern Hopfield networks. Numerical simulation confirms both the phase diagram and the convergence of the finite-size training gradient to its predicted asymptotic form.

papers.title: Einstein's theory of Brownian motion: The non-Fickian normal diffusion
papers.abstract: Einstein's theory of diffusion defines what is considered {\it normal diffusion}. Historically, Einstein considered homogeneous diffusion characterised by a diffusion constant in his original calculations, resulting in what is known as {\it Fickian} diffusion, which thermally relaxes concentration inhomogeneities. However, in the same derivation of Einstein, the seed of generalisation of the theory to {\it non-Fickian} diffusion in the presence of space-dependent diffusivity is hidden. This indicates that non-Fickian diffusion, which can drive concentration inhomogeneities, can also be normal diffusion. The present article discusses the origin of the {\it normal} non-Fickian diffusion in Einstein's theory of diffusion.

papers.title: Algebraic criteria for complete relaxation in autonomous and periodically driven open quantum systems
papers.abstract: We derive sufficient criteria that guarantee convergence of open quantum system dynamics to a unique long-time state independent of the initial conditions. We refer to this behavior as complete relaxation. Focusing on systems described by Gorini-Kossakowski-Sudarshan-Lindblad (GKSL) master equations on finite-dimensional Hilbert spaces, our approach uses only elementary mathematical arguments. For autonomous systems, we recover three previously derived relaxation criteria, which can be expressed as algebraic conditions on the Lindblad operators and the Hamiltonian entering the GKSL equation. For periodically driven systems, we obtain a new criterion involving a similar algebraic condition and a local continuity requirement on the time-dependent GKSL generator. This result implies an earlier criterion for complete relaxation formulated in Ref. [J. Phys. A 52, 43LT01 (2019)]. We also discuss implications of our approach for periodically modulated classical master equations, as well as extensions to driven systems without a periodicity constraint.

papers.title: Onsager Algebras and Lattice Fermions
papers.abstract: We study the exact Onsager algebra of free lattice fermions in staggered, Wilson, and overlap incarnations, working in both Hamiltonian and Euclidean formulations in four spacetime dimensions. In each case, we show that the exact lattice algebra emanates the full chiral symmetry of the low-energy theory: if there are $N$ massless Dirac fermions in the continuum, the Onsager algebra reduces to a $U(2N)$ chiral symmetry. The details of which generators are quantised or ultra-local differ between formulations. There is also a trade-off between the locality of generators and the maximum compact subgroup of the Onsager algebra.

papers.title: Screening strongly correlated materials in solid oxide cells with quantum simulation
papers.abstract: We develop an end-to-end framework for assessing a quantum-computing application in industrial materials science: the screening of strongly correlated oxygen-electrode materials for SOFCs and SOECs. We formulate the materials problem in terms of interface observables including oxygen-vacancy formation energies, vacancy migration barriers, and electronic conductivity. We describe how these observables can be obtained using a diagrammatic GW-based embedding, either GW+DMFT or self-energy embedding theory (SEET), applied to a DFT-screened shortlist. The atomistic electrode/electrolyte interface defines the electronic structure problem from which the correlated impurity models are constructed. Quantum impurity solvers would provide the finite-temperature impurity Green's functions required by the embedding. The computational challenges that classical solvers may encounter as the interacting active space grows, together with the polynomial scaling of quantum Hamiltonian simulation for efficiently represented discretized models, open an opportunity for quantum advantage. We identify the benchmarks needed to assess this opportunity through convergence of vacancy and migration energetics and comparison with the best applicable classical solvers. We provide illustrative logical qubit counts and identify the thermal state preparation, simulation, measurement, and repeated-solve costs needed for a complete resource assessment. We connect microscopic observables to macroscopic engineering metrics using a continuum model for mixed ionic--electronic conducting oxygen electrodes that couples oxygen surface exchange, solid-state oxygen transport, electrode microstructure, and finite electrode thickness. Finally, we estimate the potential worldwide business value of improved electrode materials under SOFC and SOEC deployment scenarios informed by public technical targets and electrolyser deployment data.

papers.title: Occupancy Driven Phase Transitions in Gapped Systems
papers.abstract: Systems characterized by an energy gap between the ground state and excited states support a growing number of thermal excitations upon raising the temperature. Provided these excitations interact with each other, their number affects the size of the energy gap akin to a harmonic oscillator where the oscillation frequency is damping dependent. Here we show that once a critical number of excitations is reached, the excitation population becomes thermodynamically unstable and the system transitions between two states. This transition is marked by a divergence in the specific heat, which does not have to be accompanied by an order parameter, nor by the full closure of the gap. We illustrate the thermodynamics using a simple two level system and superfluid $^4$He as examples, and we argue that the hidden order transition in URu$_2$Si$_2$ is an example of such an occupancy driven transition in the absence of an order parameter.

papers.title: Sign-problem-free Bosonic Auxiliary Field Quantum Monte Carlo
papers.abstract: The sign problem poses a fundamental barrier to numerically exact quantum Monte Carlo simulations, severely hindering our understanding of quantum many-body physics across disciplines ranging from condensed matter to particle and nuclear physics. Geometrical frustration makes this barrier especially acute for interacting bosons. Here, we develop a bosonic auxiliary-field quantum Monte Carlo (BAFQMC) method and rigorously prove that time-reversal symmetry and reflection positivity each provide a general sufficient condition for sign-problem-free simulations. Crucially, under either criterion, BAFQMC evades the sign problem even on frustrated lattices where conventional world-line and stochastic-series-expansion methods fail. Benchmarking our approach on a two-flavor Bose-Hubbard model on the triangular lattice yields excellent quantitative agreement with finite-temperature exact diagonalization. By establishing unifying principles to solve the sign problem in BAFQMC, our work substantially expands the reach of unbiased, numerically exact simulations for frustrated bosonic matter.

papers.title: Graph-Recurrent Learning of Emergent Collective Dynamics
papers.abstract: Collective ordering in correlated electron systems emerges from microscopic dynamics, yet the evolution of observable textures need not admit a closed, memoryless description. We introduce a graph-recurrent neural network (GRNN) framework that learns such emergent dynamics directly from trajectories without specifying microscopic equations of motion. The framework integrates gated recurrent memory with graph message passing: local hidden states encode information beyond the instantaneous observables, while spatial coupling allows this information to propagate between sites. The observable and hidden fields evolve jointly through a shared local rule, providing a scalable representation of dynamics with spatial interactions and temporal memory. We demonstrate this framework on the emergent dynamics of charge-density-wave order in the semiclassical Holstein model, successfully reproducing temporal and spatial correlations and dynamical scaling during domain coarsening. By learning finite-time evolution directly, the GRNN offers a route to efficient, data-driven descriptions of collective dynamics with unresolved microscopic degrees of freedom.

papers.title: Monodromy Defects of 3D Wilson-Fisher Criticality on the Fuzzy Sphere
papers.abstract: Monodromy (twist) line defects arise as the boundaries of topological symmetry surfaces, which are among the simplest non-trivial conformal defects with direct realizations as magnetic vortex in quantum magnets, as Wilson and t Hooft lines of gauge theories, and as the replica twist operators in quantum information theory. However, their interacting dynamics remains difficult to characterize non-perturbatively. Here we design a way to realize the monodromy boundary conditions in the fuzzy-sphere regularization by threading a symmetry-selective Aharonov-Bohm flux through the two poles of the sphere. We apply this construction to the $\mathbb{Z}_2$ twist of the 3D Ising conformal field theory (CFT), $π$-twist of the 3D O(2) CFT and three inequivalent monodromies of O(3) (centre twist, z-axis $π$-twist and the reflection). For each defect, we extract the low-lying defect spectrum together with bulk-to-defect and defect-defect operator product expansion coefficients, which characterize the operators living on the defect line, their mutual interactions, and how they couple to the surrounding critical bulk. Among the low-lying defect primaries resolved in our spectra, we find no relevant scalar perturbation that preserves all the symmetries of the corresponding defect. The relevant deformations identified in our calculations break at least one preserved symmetry, providing evidence that these monodromy defects are stable against symmetry-preserving relevant perturbations. These results establish a systematic set of non-perturbative conformal data for monodromy defects beyond the Ising twist. Our construction therefore turns the symmetry flux into a tunable knob of the fuzzy-sphere regularization, opening a route to exploring the response of critical matter to distinct defects.

papers.title: Interaction-enhanced antiferromagnetic correlations in a Kondo ladder with a gapped band structure
papers.abstract: We investigate magnetic correlations in the two-leg Kondo-Hubbard ladder using the density-matrix renormalization group method. We focus on a parameter regime in which the noninteracting electronic system has a narrow indirect band gap. In this regime, there is no Fermi surface, and the conventional Fermi-surface-based Ruderman-Kittel-Kasuya-Yosida picture is not directly applicable; magnetic correlations between localized spins become weaker as the noninteracting band gap increases. We find that a moderate on-site Coulomb interaction enhances the antiferromagnetic correlations between localized spins. This enhancement, which is also seen in the staggered magnetization induced by a pinning field at the edges, occurs for both ferromagnetic and antiferromagnetic Kondo couplings. Our results show that electron-electron interactions can enhance magnetic correlations between localized spins even when the underlying noninteracting electronic structure is gapped, suggesting an interaction-driven route to magnetic instabilities in narrow-gap Kondo-lattice systems.

papers.title: Fit-error corrected auxiliary master equation approach for low-temperature nonequilibrium dynamical mean-field theory
papers.abstract: The auxiliary master equation approach (AMEA) is a nonperturbative impurity solver for steady-state nonequilibrium dynamical mean-field theory (DMFT). It replaces the physical hybridization function by that of a small auxiliary open quantum system, whose parameters are fitted to reproduce it, and then solves the resulting many-body problem essentially exactly. AMEA's accuracy is thus limited by the quality of this fit: since the fastest-varying part of the hybridization is set by the distribution function, whose Fermi edges sharpen at low temperature, the fit tends to overestimate the temperature, especially for weak reservoir coupling. For the auxiliary hybridization itself, however, AMEA's self-energy is essentially exact. We correct for the fit error by estimating, via an approximate solver applicable to arbitrary hybridization functions, the ratio between the self-energies of the physical and auxiliary hybridizations, and using it to extend AMEA's self-energy from the auxiliary to the physical case. This fit-error correction becomes exact whenever either the fit or the approximate solver is exact. We benchmark the scheme using the nonequilibrium Kajueter-Kotliar iterated perturbation theory (IPT), generalized here to spin-polarized solutions, as the approximate solver; other approximate solvers, such as the noncrossing approximation, can be used as well. Applied to an Anderson impurity model with a spin-polarized bath, and within DMFT to a Hubbard layer weakly coupled to two metallic reservoirs, the correction largely removes the spurious heating from the AMEA fit and from insufficient thermalization by the reservoirs, while preserving the correct description of the Mott insulator, which IPT alone cannot fully recover.

papers.title: Anyon Chern bands of opposite sign and reversed drift
papers.abstract: The elementary charged excitations of fractional quantum Hall states are anyons. Without continuous translation symmetry, they acquire a dispersion and richer dynamics. We study the Laughlin quasihole at filling $1/3$ in a periodically modulated magnetic field, a common model of fractional Chern insulators in two-dimensional materials. From the microscopic wave functions, we derive the commutator of its guiding-center coordinates, set by a many-body Berry curvature that governs its wave packets. A modulation with two flux quanta per unit cell splits the quasihole band into bands with Chern numbers $6$ and $-3$; such opposite signs are generic as long as a weak modulation opens a gap between the anyon bands. In the $C=-3$ band, the quasihole drifts against $\mathbf{E}\times\mathbf{B}$, although the magnetic field has the same sign everywhere. Perturbation theory in the modulation explains these results, and large-scale Monte Carlo calculations confirm them. Anyon bands thus acquire their own topology, which controls anyon motion and may shape the phases of itinerant anyons.

papers.title: Impact of localized $4f$ magnetism on Berry curvature and the intrinsic anomalous Hall effect in CeRu$_2$Si$_2$
papers.abstract: The intrinsic anomalous Hall effect (AHE), originating from Berry curvature, has been extensively studied in $f$-electron systems, including Ce-based compounds. However, how the magnetism of localized $f$ electrons affect the intrinsic AHE remains unclear. Here, we investigate this issue in CeRu$_2$Si$_2$ by calculating the intrinsic anomalous Hall conductivity (AHC) for several occupied Ce-$4f$ states using first-principles LDA+$U$ calculations combined with Wannier interpolation method. We find that the intrinsic AHC remains finite even when the Ce-$4f$ states are localized and do not contribute directly to the Fermi surface, and that its magnitude depends on which Ce-$4f$ state is occupied. We show that localized $4f$-electron magnetism induces exchange splitting in the conduction bands, generating Berry curvature in specific regions near the Fermi surface. This mechanism enables conduction bands that are derived from nonmagnetic orbitals and form the Fermi surface to contribute to the intrinsic AHE, suggesting a route to realizing large intrinsic AHE in $f$-electron materials.

papers.title: String Order in Quench Dynamics as a Probe of Quantum Phase Transitions
papers.abstract: We study the anisotropic XY chain in a transverse field by introducing a global string order parameter and examining its equilibrium behavior and its quench dynamics from a fully polarized initial state. The corresponding string operator is defined as the product of local projected spin operators over the entire chain. The nonequilibrium order parameter is the long-time average of the logarithm of the string-operator expectation value per site after the quench.For the ground state, its field derivative is singular on the Ising critical lines; after the quench, the steady-state response also records the field boundaries and the anisotropy transition. We derive analytically the nonanalytic behavior of the order parameter at the quantum critical lines. Our results reveal a hidden nonlocal order underlying this paradigmatic model of conventional quantum phase transitions. They also connect measurable spin populations with equilibrium and dynamical topological structure.

papers.title: Anisotropic thermoelectric transport in the Sr2RuO4-Ru eutectic system
papers.abstract: The Sr2RuO4-Ru eutectic system, in which metallic Ru inclusions are embedded in a Sr2RuO4 matrix, exhibits an enhanced superconducting onset temperature of about 3 K, known as the 3-K phase. Here we investigate the in-plane thermoelectric response of this eutectic system in the normal state and find a pronounced anisotropy in the thermopower for thermal gradients applied parallel and perpendicular to the Ru lamellae. To clarify its origin, we combine thermopower measurements with electronic-structure-based transport calculations and finite-element modeling of the local strain distribution generated by the thermal-expansion mismatch between Sr2RuO4 and Ru. The calculations show that uniaxial compression of Sr2RuO4 produces a sizable thermopower anisotropy through modification of the Fermi surfaces. When an idealized spatially inhomogeneous strain field around the Ru lamellae is included, the observed sign and qualitative magnitude of the anisotropy are reproduced more closely than in a simple unstrained two-component model. These results are consistent with a substantial contribution from strain-induced changes in the Sr2RuO4 electronic structure near the interfaces, although contributions from interfacial phase mixing and three-dimensional transport connectivity cannot be excluded.

papers.title: Mixed State Deep Thermalization under Generic Quantum Errors
papers.abstract: Pure-state deep thermalization predicts that, after sufficient scrambling, projected ensembles approach universal distributions that contain information beyond the reduced density matrix. In realistic quantum systems, however, noise is unavoidable and the projected states are generally mixed. Whether mixed-state deep thermalization admits an analogous universal limiting distribution has remained unclear. Here we answer this question for quantum dynamics containing local quantum channels, i.e., errors. We show that the late-time mixed-state projected ensemble is completely determined by the normalized Choi state of the error channel and is universal, independent of the microscopic details of the underlying unitary dynamics. We establish this result analytically for dual-unitary circuits, global Haar-random dynamics, and local Haar-random circuits at large local dimension, and verify it numerically in qubit circuits and kicked Ising dynamics. In a solvable setting, we further find exponentially fast convergence to the limiting ensemble. Our results extend deep thermalization to noisy quantum dynamics and establish a direct correspondence between quantum errors and universal random mixed-state ensembles.

papers.title: Orbital-coherence memory in electrical transport and its self-consistent Maxwell response
papers.abstract: An internal electronic coherence changes electrical transport only when it feeds back on the physical current. We develop a reduced description of this feedback and distinguish its exact consequences from the assumptions required for a microscopic realization. An opposite-parity two-orbital Hamiltonian identifies a current-coupled orbital force. Under an explicitly stated moment closure and collision ansatz, it yields a passive three-state response with an exponentially damped oscillatory memory. The resulting conductivity redistributes a fixed optical weight and predicts a nonmonotonic dependence of dc conduction on coherence damping at fixed remaining parameters. The orbital reduction constrains the coupling and internal frequency through a shared bare splitting, providing a test beyond unconstrained spectral fitting.
